description: I'm a 10-year-old space enthusiast doing a solo project for "Abandoned but not Forgotten." My skill is creative storytelling—I'm making an interactive map of NASA's abandoned space equipment using a funny "Mom telling you to clean your room" theme! I need teammates (older students/adults) who can help with web design/coding, graphic design, or video presentation. If you love space and want to help a kid build something fun and unique, join my team!
summary:
I made "The Cosmic Chore" an interactive map of the things NASA has left behind in space. It covers 13 objects in three places, and each place is a room in a house. The Moon is the Backyard, Mars is the Attic, and Deep Space is the Closet.

When you click a pin, a speech bubble pops up. The top part is Mom nagging, like "You drove three electric moon buggies and parked them permanently on the Moon? Did you even check for parking tickets?" The bottom part says what the object really is, using NASA's own descriptions.

My project takes NASA's list of objects and turns it into a story that kids and parents understand right away. Everyone knows what it's like when Mom tells you to clean your room. So it's easy to remember that rovers, landers, a helicopter and telescopes are still out there.

This matters because space exploration leaves things behind. If kids learn about it in a fun way, they will care about exploring space responsibly when they grow up.
details:
What it does: The Cosmic Chore is an interactive PowerPoint map of 13 objects NASA left in space. The Moon is the Backyard, Mars is the Attic, and Deep Space is the Closet. Click a pin to open that room. Each object's card shows Mom nagging on top and NASA's real description below.

Benefits: It's easy to understand, because everyone has been told to clean their room. The facts are accurate because they're NASA's own words. You explore it by clicking, and it only needs PowerPoint.

Intended impact: People learn that space exploration leaves things behind, and they remember it. Kids may then grow up to plan cleaner missions.

Tools: Microsoft PowerPoint on a Windows laptop. My parents expertise in designing Interactive PPT. We used the NASA Space Apps brand guide and logos, the Fira Sans and Overpass fonts, Phosphor icons, and NASA's list of objects.

Creativity: We turned a NASA list into a story with Mom as the main character. You laugh at the nagging first, then learn the fact.

Factors considered:

Accuracy: NASA's words are kept exactly.

Audience: the text is simple and easy for kids to read.

Brand: we followed the Space Apps brand rules.

Readability: high-contrast colors work on a projector.

Length: it fits in 7 slides.

Any computer: the fonts are embedded so the text shows correctly everywhere.
